Services

Every blade, done right

From the knife block in your kitchen to the blade in your tackle box — if it’s meant to cut, it can be brought back. All brands welcome.

Kitchen & Chef Knives

Chef’s knives, santoku, paring, boning, and fillet knives restored to a clean, even edge — the workhorses of gumbo night, Sunday sauce, and everyday cooking.

Cutco & Double-D® Edge

Cutco’s recessed Double-D® edge takes the right touch to sharpen without ruining the pattern. It’s a specialty of the house — your Cutco set, handled the way Cutco owners hope for.

Specialty

Serrated Blades

Bread knives, steak knives, and serrated utility blades — yes, serrated can be sharpened. Each tooth is dressed so the blade bites and slices clean again instead of tearing.

Yes — serrated too

Hunting & Outdoor Knives

Skinning, gut-hook, and camp knives sharpened for the season — deer camp, duck blinds, and cleaning fish at the dock. A working edge that holds up in the field.

Pocket Knives & Everyday Carry

The folder in your pocket and the multi-tool in your truck deserve a real edge too. Folding and fixed blades, touched up and ready for daily work.

Repair — Tips & Chips

Broken tip from a drop on the tile? Chips from a bone or a frozen roast? Damaged blades are re-profiled and the tip rebuilt, then sharpened like the rest.

How Mobile Sharpening Works

No drop-off. No shipping. He comes to you.

Cajun Knife Sharpening runs on routes across the Lafayette area. Here’s how a visit comes together:

01

Call or Text

Reach Jordan at (337) 349-9776 and say what you’ve got — a full knife block, a Cutco set, a hunting blade, or one sad bread knife.

02

Get on the Route

He’ll let you know when he’ll be in your area and set a time that works. Mobile and by appointment — that’s the whole model.

03

Sharpened On Site

Your knives are sharpened right there at your home or business — no mailing your good blades across the country and waiting a week.

04

Pay & Cook

Settle up on the spot, and your knives go straight back to work — thinner tomato slices, cleaner cuts, safer cooking.

About the Sharpener

Jordan McGee of Eunice, Louisiana

Cajun Knife Sharpening is Jordan McGee of Eunice, Louisiana — a craftsman who turned an obsession with a true edge into a mobile service for Acadiana. He’s listed as a knife sharpener with the Louisiana Custom Knife Association, in the company of the state’s custom makers and bladesmiths.

Instead of a storefront you have to drive to, Jordan brings the bench to you — kitchens, camps, and businesses across the Lafayette area. One person, start to finish: the hands that answer your call are the hands on the stone.

  • Local & accountable — based right in Eunice, not a mail-in warehouse.
  • Edges matched to the blade — a fillet knife, a chef’s knife, and a hunting blade don’t get the same treatment.
  • Specialty edges welcome — Cutco Double-D®, serrated, and damaged blades included.

Made for Louisiana Kitchens

Sharp knives are Cajun cooking equipment

Around here, a knife isn’t decoration. It breaks down the trinity for the gumbo pot, fillets redfish and specs at the cleaning table, slices boudin and andouille, and works through a sack of crawfish-season prep. Cooking like this wears an edge down fast — and a dull knife makes every one of those jobs harder and more dangerous.

That’s why the service is mobile and local: when the knives at home, at the camp, or in your restaurant kitchen go dull, help is one call away — from somebody who cooks the same food you do.

Questions

Before you call

Do you sharpen serrated knives?+

Yes. Serrated blades — bread knives, steak knives, serrated utility and tomato knives — are sharpened tooth by tooth so they bite cleanly again instead of tearing. It’s one of the most common questions on the Facebook page, and the answer is always yes.

Do you sharpen Cutco knives and the Double-D® edge?+

Yes — Cutco is a specialty. The Double-D® edge has recessed cutting edges with protected points, and sharpening it correctly takes a specific approach so the pattern isn’t ground away. Straight-edge Cutco blades are sharpened like any fine kitchen knife.

Do you really come to me?+

Yes — it’s a mobile service, based in Eunice and running routes across the Lafayette area and greater Acadiana. Call or text, and Jordan will let you know when he’ll be in your area and set up a time. Sharpening is done on site, by appointment.

What brands do you sharpen?+

Just about all of them — Cutco, the big German and Japanese kitchen brands, American hunting and pocket knife brands, and plenty of no-name workhorses besides. If it has an edge, ask. The honest answer is almost always yes.

Can you fix a broken tip or a chipped blade?+

Yes. Tip and chip repair is part of the service: the blade is re-profiled, the tip rebuilt, and the edge re-established, then sharpened and finished like any other knife. Send a photo by text if you want a straight answer on a badly damaged blade before booking.

How do I book, and how does payment work?+

Call or text (337) 349-9776, say what you’ve got and where you are, and you’ll be added to the route for your area. You pay when the work is done — and your knives go straight back into the block, sharp.
